description: A log replayed through a rulebook gives one row per event with the decision's status and reasons, totals by status, and counts by area, by role and by rule; the fingerprint names the rulebook that decided.

builtin.text: Every fact a decision needs must be supplied and valid; a missing or invalid fact is never permission.
Only declared areas are governed; anything in an undeclared area is blocked.
Only declared roles may act; unknown roles are blocked.
A participant may only take actions its role lists.
An action the rulebook does not know is denied, or waits for approval, as the rulebook says (otherwise).
A plan step happens where the earlier steps left the participant unless its action moves it there.

findings.message: `alarm_allows_look` set by low tries to loosen what `yard_closed_at_night` set by high sets: `alarm_allows_look` (set by low) says allow; `yard_closed_at_night` (set by high) says deny. Both apply to every role · look · Yard, when time in 00:00–06:00, 20:00–24:00 and alarm in true. A lower authority can only tighten, so `alarm_allows_look` never takes effect there. For example: bot does look in yard with people=0, day="mon", time="00:00", alarm=true.

`alarm_allows_look` set by low tries to loosen what `four_looks_an_hour` set by high sets: `alarm_allows_look` (set by low) says allow; `four_looks_an_hour` (set by high) says deny. Both apply to every role · look · everywhere, when alarm in true. A lower authority can only tighten, so `alarm_allows_look` never takes effect at all. (Overlap is possible, not proven: a rule here conditions on history, which the analysis does not model; on the facts alone both would match bot does look in floor with people=0, time="00:00", day="mon", alarm=true.)

`no_look_in_alarm` (set by high) is already covered by `four_looks_an_hour` (set by high), which says the same thing (deny) for every role · look · everywhere, when alarm in true. `no_look_in_alarm` adds nothing. (Overlap is possible, not proven: a rule here conditions on history, which the analysis does not model; on the facts alone both would match bot does look in floor with people=0, time="00:00", day="mon", alarm=true.)

Only declared areas are governed; anything in an undeclared area is blocked.
Only declared roles may act; unknown roles are blocked.
A participant may only take actions its role lists.
An action the rulebook does not know is denied, or waits for approval, as the rulebook says (otherwise).
A plan step happens where the earlier steps left the participant unless its action moves it there.

findings.message: `alarm_allows_look` set by low tries to loosen what `yard_closed_at_night` set by high sets: `alarm_allows_look` (set by low) says allow; `yard_closed_at_night` (set by high) says deny. Both apply to every role · look · Yard, when time in 00:00–06:00, 20:00–24:00 and alarm in true. A lower authority can only tighten, so `alarm_allows_look` never takes effect there. For example: bot does look in yard with people=0, day="mon", time="00:00", alarm=true.

`alarm_allows_look` set by low tries to loosen what `four_looks_an_hour` set by high sets: `alarm_allows_look` (set by low) says allow; `four_looks_an_hour` (set by high) says deny. Both apply to every role · look · everywhere, when alarm in true. A lower authority can only tighten, so `alarm_allows_look` never takes effect at all. (Overlap is possible, not proven: a rule here conditions on history, which the analysis does not model; on the facts alone both would match bot does look in floor with people=0, time="00:00", day="mon", alarm=true.)

`no_look_in_alarm` (set by high) is already covered by `four_looks_an_hour` (set by high), which says the same thing (deny) for every role · look · everywhere, when alarm in true. `no_look_in_alarm` adds nothing. (Overlap is possible, not proven: a rule here conditions on history, which the analysis does not model; on the facts alone both would match bot does look in floor with people=0, time="00:00", day="mon", alarm=true.)

`alarm_allows_look` set by low tries to loosen what `no_look_in_alarm` set by high sets: `alarm_allows_look` (set by low) says allow; `no_look_in_alarm` (set by high) says deny. Both apply to every role · look · everywhere, when alarm in true. A lower authority can only tighten, so `alarm_allows_look` never takes effect at all. For example: bot does look in floor with people=0, time="00:00", day="mon", alarm=true.
